speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your response. To better understand your neck and arm symptoms, can you describe what the pain feels like and whether it radiates down your arm or into your hand? Also, have you noticed any recent trauma or repetitive strain activities?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning pain and progressive hand weakness over three months, combined with your history of diabetes and hypertension, strongly suggest cervical radiculopathy or a compressive myelopathy. Is the weakness more prominent in your hands or does it also affect your legs or balance? Additionally, could you point to exactly which fingers are numb or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) with suspected C5-C6 cord compression.

Given the progressive weakness, absent reflexes, and fasciculations alongside your diabetes, I need to confirm spinal cord compression before proceeding. REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI results.
